clue.text: Drive a distance in Selkirk, say

parts.note: to cast out is to drive away, so cast can mean drive
far off, at a distance, is away

explanation.surface: A golfer hitting a long tee shot in the Scottish border town of Selkirk.
explanation.walkthrough: Selkirk looks like the Borders town, but it is Alexander Selkirk, the marooned sailor whose story inspired Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Selkirk was marooned alone on a Pacific island for four years, the model of a shipwrecked survivor.

clue.text: I leave broken biscuit for Picasso, for example

indicators.note: the letter I leaves and what remains is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the letter I itself, taken out

explanation.surface: Picasso walking off and leaving a biscuit in pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from BISCUIT to get BSCUIT, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism, the art movement of fragmented geometric forms.

clue.text: Battle raging on street

indicators.note: in a down clue the raging word sits on, after, the street, so it comes second

parts.note: a disease raging through a town is rife, widespread

explanation.surface: A fierce battle raging in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or fighting.

clue.text: A banger, we hear, in a pile?

parts.note: we hear people call an old banger, a worn-out car, a heap

explanation.surface: Someone hearing an old car and wondering if it's a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a rickety old car, also called a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Aheap is an old word for gathered together in a mound.

clue.text: A shilling below rent?

parts.note: s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
under means beneath, below

explanation.surface: A tenant paying a shilling less than the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past participle of rend, torn. The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means torn apart into pieces, as something rent has been.

clue.text: Polish area of car damaged at Hereford, possibly?

indicators.note: a damaged car is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Hereford is a breed of cattle, so one example is a cow

explanation.surface: A car wrecked in the English town of Hereford, in some Polish district.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford reads as the English city, but here it is the beef breed. Polish is the nationality, not shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Krakow, once spelt Cracow in English, is a city and region in southern Poland.

clue.text: Castles surrounding lake provide noisy nesting-grounds

indicators.note: surrounding means the castles go round the lake

parts.note: a rook is the chess piece also called a castle
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Castles around a lake where birds nest noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castles' paints buildings, but it means chess rooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rookeries are colonies of rooks, crows that nest together in loud treetop colonies.

clue.text: Was it kindled by a gay spark?

definitions.text: Was it kindled by a gay spark?

parts.words: Was it kindled by a gay spark?
parts.note: a gay spark is a merry fellow, but also a bright flying ember that sets an outdoor blaze going; camp also means flamboyantly gay

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a cheerful young man lit the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air fire at a camp is lit from sparks, and camp also means flamboyant.

clue.text: Fatigue? Short of energy? Caution!

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: fatigue is weariness, tiredness
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired person running out of energy is told to be careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness is caution, a guarded watchfulness.

clue.text: Wine from a rude box?

indicators.note: the wine is made from these letters, which are reworked to produce it

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine arriving in a crude crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret from the Bordeaux region of France is a famous red wine.

clue.text: In quest of half summer past

parts.note: going for something means seeking it, so for means in quest of

indicators.note: only the second half of the word summer is used here

explanation.surface: Seeking half a summer that has already gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something former belonged to an earlier time, now gone by.

clue.text: Joy of early music

explanation.surface: The delight of hearing old music.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is delight; a glee is also a part-song for unaccompanied voices, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Adopt self-regulating volume-control

indicators.note: regulating means putting in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to install an automatic volume control.
explanation.walkthrough: Self-regulating looks like one adjective; split it, so 'regulating' works on ADOPT SELF.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft pedal of a piano quietens its tone, a control of loudness.

clue.text: Mischievous, small German eleven at home

parts.note: elf is the German word for the number eleven
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: A small, naughty German football team playing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German eleven' suggests a football side; it is the German number word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are tiny, impish folk, so elfin describes something little and playfully naughty.

clue.text: A pot slightly open

parts.note: a pot and a jar are both containers

explanation.surface: A slightly open pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left a little open is described as ajar.

clue.text: Tender, cheerful craft

parts.note: jolly means cheerful
a craft is a vessel, a boat

explanation.surface: A gentle, merry vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective meaning gentle; it is a small boat serving a larger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A jollyboat is a small ship's boat, a tender used for ferrying.

clue.text: They go abroad and see grim changes

indicators.note: grim changes means the letters of the phrase are altered in order

explanation.surface: Emigrants leave their country and witness bleak changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigres are people who have left their homeland to live overseas.

clue.text: Narcissus possibly held a pose endlessly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way
endlessly means the last letter of pose is dropped

explanation.surface: Narcissus, admiring himself, perhaps struck a pose without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Narcissus suggests the youth who loved his reflection; here it is the flower. 'endlessly' trims POSE to POS before 'possibly' rearranges HELD A POS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-family flower, and the narcissus or daffodil was historically called by that name.

clue.text: Relaxed? Spar and stall!

parts.note: loose means relaxed, not tight
to spar is to box, fight with fists in practice

explanation.surface: A relaxed boxer sparring before a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A loosebox is a stable compartment where a horse can move about untied.

clue.text: Lowered section-leader fitted with hood

indicators.note: the leader of the section is its opening letter

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood, so one fitted with it is cowled

explanation.surface: A section leader who dropped down and put on a hood.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowered is not 'let down' but the verb to lour (lower), meaning to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower, also spelt lour, means to frown or look sullen.

clue.text: Bird no longer has dual function

indicators.note: dual means two, so the word for function appears twice

parts.note: a do is a party, a social function

explanation.surface: An extinct bird with a twofold purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Cut free

explanation.surface: A cut, given for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a deep wound; as naval slang, gash means spare or surplus, there for nothing.

clue.text: Tough-looking guy who minds a primate

explanation.surface: A heavy bodyguard compared to an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is slang for a burly minder or thug; it is also the largest ape.

clue.text: Dressing down a sailor…

explanation.surface: A sailor being scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a reprimand, a telling-off; a rating is also a non-officer seaman.

clue.text: … gadabout in rough sea (Proverbs)

indicators.note: the gadabout sits inside the rough sea
rough water is churned, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: read as gad about, the word gad turned round

explanation.surface: A wanderer out on rough water among the sayings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gadabout' gives GAD turned round by 'about'; 'rough' works on SEA. Proverbs is not the Bible book but sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are traditional sayings expressing common wisdom.

clue.text: Rapid way in country dance

indicators.note: the way sits inside the dance

parts.note: the hay is an old English country dance
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A quick route in some rustic dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The HAY (or hey) is a traditional English country dance with weaving figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means done quickly, in a hurry.

clue.text: Suspended target of English river authority

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, south-west England
a board is a governing body, an authority

explanation.surface: A water board for an English river whose target has been suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended' suggests a halted plan; it means hung on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard hangs on a wall as the thing players throw darts at.

clue.text: To mingle, bishop needs to advance

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A bishop has to make a loan in order to socialise.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend is to mix or combine things together.

clue.text: Society-girl with a rise becomes a borrower

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering high society
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A debutante whose social rise leaves her owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor owes money, having borrowed it.

clue.text: Navy calling at Gateshead (Here today, gone tomorrow)

parts.note: a fleet is a navy's body of ships
a ship calling at a port puts in, so in
read as Gate's head, the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: Warships putting in at Gateshead, a town on the Tyne, and leaving quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split it as Gate's head for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means brief and passing, lasting only a short while.

clue.text: Slackness of a number among non-clergy

indicators.note: among means the number is placed inside the lay people

parts.note: the laity are people who are not clergy
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Lax standards among a congregation of lay people.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is a lack of strictness or care, a looseness.

clue.text: Measurements of London police taking an awfully long time

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, headquarters of the Metropolitan Police
ages is a colloquial phrase for a very long time

explanation.surface: London detectives taking forever over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardages are lengths measured in yards.
